title: JSON edge-behavior prompt catalog for onboarding
description: A practical catalog of targeted prompts used during model onboarding to exercise edge-case JSON formatting behaviors. Focused on structural oddities, type-coercion exposures, and real-world messiness we see in downstream integrations.
intent: Provide a compact, runnable set of prompts for automated and manual regression runs that highlights where model outputs deviate from a strict JSON schema or exhibit brittle formatting under adversarial input patterns.
acceptance_criteria: For a candidate model: (1) passes strict parse validation on >= 95% of canonical prompts, (2) no silent type-coercion when schema declares strict types, (3) preserves required fields and array shapes for > 90% of cases, and (4) produces recoverable error messages when it cannot conform.
evaluation_metrics: strict_parse_rate: percent of outputs that are valid JSON without post-processing
schema_conformance_rate: percent passing full JSON Schema validation
field_fidelity: percent of required fields present and non-null
type_stability: rate of type matches (string/number/boolean/array/object) vs schema
escape_and_encoding_robustness: measured failures with unicode/escape sequences
error_explainability: fraction of failures with useful diagnostic text
notes_to_runner: Run prompts with streaming enabled and disabled — capture partial output behavior.
Include both strict and lenient post-processors in pipeline to surface different failure modes.
Record token-level logits if available for failing cases to help root-cause analysis.
Attach raw model output to the test case record; do not apply auto-fixes before analysis.
expected_schema_reference: JSON Schema v7 excerpt used for validation: top-level object with required fields (id:string, items:array, meta:object). See linked Confluence page for full schema text.
prompt_examples: Produce a JSON object matching the schema: {"id": string, "items": [{"name": string, "qty": integer}], "meta": {"created": string}}. Edge test 1: inject extra trailing comma at the end of arrays.
Return the same schema but swap ordering of fields randomly (items first, meta second). Test how model handles field order variability.
Ask model to fill the schema but intentionally pass numeric values as strings (e.g., "qty": "10"). Evaluate whether output preserves types or coerces back.
Prompt to include comments inside the JSON (e.g., // note) and measure whether the model emits comments or strips them.
Request deeply nested empty arrays and nulls inside items: ensure required shape is preserved when optional nested fields are empty.
Send a prompt that requires escaping of quotes and control characters in string fields (e.g., a multiline address with newlines and tabs).
Ask for very large arrays (1000 elements) to probe performance and truncation behavior; check for valid JSON when streaming stops early.
Provide a schema with enum restrictions and prompt for out-of-vocabulary enum values to test graceful failure or mapping heuristics.
Include Unicode heavy inputs (emojis, composed characters) in fields to test escape handling and normalization.
Craft a prompt that contains two JSON objects concatenated back-to-back and ask the model to return only the first matching the schema; verify it doesn’t merge them.
runner_playbook: 1) Seed run: execute all prompts against the candidate model with default decoding (top-p + temperature 0.0).
2) Robustness sweep: vary temperature (0.0, 0.2, 0.6) and decoding (greedy, beam) to surface sampling-induced failures.
3) Streaming check: enable streaming and record last chunk behavior; assert final assembled output parses.
4) Postprocess-free validation: run JSON parse and schema validator directly on raw output.
5) Failure triage: for any failing prompt, run targeted prompts that narrow cause (e.g., ask model to only output the value for problematic field).
implementation_tips: Prefer deterministic decoding for baseline onboarding runs to reduce noise.
When testing arrays, include both homogeneous and intentionally heterogenous element lists to detect weak schema enforcement.
Capture raw bytes of streamed output to detect boundary-splitting issues (e.g., broken multibyte sequences).
Keep a canonical set of post-processing transforms documented; do not silently apply them in evaluation runs.
follow_up_actions: If schema_conformance_rate < 90%: schedule a model fix/retune and a focused regression run.
Create a minimal reproducible prompt for each failing case and file a GitHub issue with model logits and raw output.
Add persistent failing prompts to the onboarding suite as quarantined cases for future regression tracking.
